caption: A baked potato fresh from the oven is split open with a fork, and steam rises from the white flesh inside.

sa.check: The potato is split open with a fork.
Steam rises from the flesh inside.
The flesh inside is white and fluffy.
The split comes first and the steam follows.

pc.expect: The steam appears from the cut faces at the moment the potato opens and not from the unbroken skin.
pc.fail: Steam rises from the whole potato before it is opened; or the potato is opened and no steam appears from the cut to the end of the clip; or steam pours from the unbroken skin while the cut faces are clear; or steam appears above the potato with nothing leaving the cut.

pc.expect: The steam rises from the cut faces, spreading and thinning as it climbs.
pc.fail: The steam sinks onto the plate and pools; or pours downward out of the cut; or hangs as a fixed shape without rising; or flows sideways with nothing blowing it.

pc.expect: The skin is a tough shell that tears along the fork's line and the flesh inside is soft and crumbly, while the fork stays rigid.
pc.fail: The skin stretches like rubber as the fork goes in; or the flesh runs out as a liquid; or the potato splits as a brittle shell into sharp shards; or the fork bends.

pc.expect: The split only opens wider and the steam only leaves; the potato does not close up again.
pc.fail: The split closes and the potato is whole again; or the cut faces knit back together; or the steam runs back into the potato; or the flesh draws back inside the skin.

pc.expect: One potato and one fork; the potato stays one potato in two halves and nothing passes through the plate.
pc.fail: A second potato appears; or the potato vanishes; or the fork passes through the plate; or the halves merge into a whole potato with no seam.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The plate, the potato's skin away from the cut and the table stay the same.
pc.fail: The plate changes pattern; or the skin changes colour away from the cut; or items on the table rearrange.
